paper.title_en: Reservoir-Engineered Josephson Diode in a Dark Andreev Channel
paper.abstract_en: We propose a reservoir-engineered Josephson diode in a double-dot junction with symmetric coherent couplings. A relative phase in the coupling to a common loss reservoir selects a rapidly decaying bright orbital and an orthogonal dark Andreev channel. In the quantum Zeno regime, virtual bright-sector transitions set the dark-channel occupation while preserving its coherent supercurrent. For junctions in the infinite-gap Zeno regime, the steady-state current factorizes as $I_{\rm ss}=I_A P_γ$: a reciprocal spectral current $I_A$ is reweighted by the reservoir-selected occupation imbalance $P_γ$, which generates rectification. The resulting nonreciprocal current remains finite as reservoir leakage decreases with increasing loss strength. Furthermore, local Coulomb repulsion tunes a dark-pair resonance that enables near-ideal rectification, with induced two-particle loss essential to the quantitative description of the steady current. Keldysh-Lindblad calculations confirm that the results remain robust at finite loss strength and superconducting gap.
